question: How much revenue have we made?

gold_sql.sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount),0) FROM payments WHERE status='succeeded' AND currency='USD'
gold_sql.label: revenue_gross
gold_sql.clarification_answer: Gross succeeded USD payments, no refund deduction

gold_sql.sql:
SELECT COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount) FROM payments WHERE status='succeeded' AND currency='USD'),0)
                   - COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount) FROM refunds WHERE currency='USD'),0)
gold_sql.label: revenue_net

baseline_sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM("p"."amount") FILTER(WHERE "p"."status" = 'succeeded'), 0) - COALESCE(SUM("r"."amount"), 0) AS "revenue_net" FROM "orders" AS "o" LEFT JOIN "payments" AS "p" ON "o"."id" = "p"."order_id" AND "p"."currency" = 'USD' LEFT JOIN "refunds" AS "r" ON "o"."id" = "r"."order_id" AND "r"."currency" = 'USD' LEFT JOIN "users" AS "u" ON "o"."user_id" = "u"."id" WHERE "o"."status" <> 'cancelled' AND "u"."is_internal" = FALSE AND "u"."deleted_at" IS NULL LIMIT 1000
resolved_sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM("p"."amount") FILTER(WHERE "p"."status" = 'succeeded'), 0) - COALESCE(SUM("r"."amount"), 0) AS "revenue_net" FROM "orders" AS "o" LEFT JOIN "payments" AS "p" ON "o"."id" = "p"."order_id" AND "p"."currency" = 'USD' LEFT JOIN "refunds" AS "r" ON "o"."id" = "r"."order_id" AND "r"."currency" = 'USD' LEFT JOIN "users" AS "u" ON "o"."user_id" = "u"."id" WHERE "o"."status" <> 'cancelled' AND "u"."is_internal" = FALSE AND "u"."deleted_at" IS NULL LIMIT 1000

question: List our best-selling products.

gold_sql.sql:
SELECT products.id, products.name, SUM(order_items.unit_price*order_items.quantity) AS revenue
            FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.id
            GROUP BY products.id, products.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5
gold_sql.label: top_5

gold_sql.sql:
SELECT products.id, products.name, SUM(order_items.unit_price*order_items.quantity) AS revenue
            FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.id
            GROUP BY products.id, products.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10
gold_sql.label: top_10

baseline_sql: SELECT "p"."id" AS "id", "p"."name" AS "name", "c"."name" AS "category", SUM("oi"."quantity") AS "total_units_sold" FROM "products" AS "p" JOIN "categories" AS "c" ON "p"."category_id" = "c"."id" JOIN "order_items" AS "oi" ON "p"."id" = "oi"."product_id" JOIN "orders" AS "o" ON "oi"."order_id" = "o"."id" WHERE "p"."deleted_at" IS NULL AND "o"."status" <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY "p"."id", "p"."name", "c"."name" ORDER BY "total_units_sold" DESC LIMIT 10
resolved_sql: SELECT "p"."id" AS "id", "p"."name" AS "name", "c"."name" AS "category", COALESCE(SUM("oi"."quantity"), 0) AS "units_sold", COALESCE(SUM("oi"."quantity" * "oi"."unit_price"), 0) - COALESCE((SELECT SUM("r"."amount") AS "_col_0" FROM "refunds" AS "r" WHERE "r"."order_id" = "o"."id" AND "r"."currency" = 'USD'), 0) AS "revenue_net" FROM "products" AS "p" LEFT JOIN "order_items" AS "oi" ON "p"."id" = "oi"."product_id" LEFT JOIN "orders" AS "o" ON "oi"."order_id" = "o"."id" LEFT JOIN "categories" AS "c" ON "p"."category_id" = "c"."id" WHERE "p"."deleted_at" IS NULL AND "o"."status" <> 'cancelled' AND "o"."status" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY "p"."id", "p"."name", "c"."name" ORDER BY "revenue_net" DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

question: How many customers do we have?

gold_sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND is_internal = false
gold_sql.label: users_table
gold_sql.clarification_answer: Active, non-internal login accounts (the users table)

baseline_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "customers"."id") AS "customer_count" FROM "customers" AS "customers" LIMIT 1000
resolved_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "u"."customer_id") AS "customer_count" FROM "users" AS "u" WHERE "u"."is_internal" = FALSE AND "u"."deleted_at" IS NULL LIMIT 1000

question: How many orders came in this quarter?

gold_sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2025-10-01' AND created_at < '2026-01-01'
gold_sql.label: calendar_quarter

gold_sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE created_at >= (SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM orders) - INTERVAL '90 days'
gold_sql.label: trailing_90_days
gold_sql.clarification_answer: Trailing 90 days from the most recent order

baseline_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "orders"."id") AS "order_count" FROM "orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."status" <> 'cancelled' AND DATE_TRUNC('QUARTER', "orders"."created_at") = DATE_TRUNC('QUARTER', (SELECT MAX("orders"."created_at") AS "_col_0" FROM "orders" AS "orders")) LIMIT 1000
resolved_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "orders"."id") AS "order_count" FROM "orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."status" <> 'cancelled' AND DATE_TRUNC('QUARTER', "orders"."created_at") = DATE_TRUNC('QUARTER', (SELECT MAX("orders"."created_at") AS "_col_0" FROM "orders" AS "orders")) LIMIT 1000

question: What's the average number of failed payment attempts per order, among orders that ever had one?

gold_sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FROM payments WHERE status = 'failed'
gold_sql.label: per_order
gold_sql.clarification_answer: Failed payment rows / distinct orders with >=1 failed payment

gold_sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*)::numeric / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FROM payments WHERE status = 'failed') FROM payments WHERE status = 'failed'
gold_sql.label: per_failed_row
gold_sql.clarification_answer: Same count expressed per failed-payment row (each row is one order)

baseline_sql: SELECT AVG("orders_with_failures"."failed_count") AS "avg_failed_payments_per_order" FROM (SELECT "orders"."id" AS "id", COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE "payments"."status" = 'failed') AS "failed_count" FROM "orders" AS "orders" JOIN "payments" AS "payments" ON "orders"."id" = "payments"."order_id" WHERE "orders"."status" <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY "orders"."id" HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE "payments"."status" = 'failed') > 0) AS "orders_with_failures" LIMIT 1000
resolved_sql: SELECT AVG("orders_with_failures"."failed_count") AS "avg_failed_payments_per_order" FROM (SELECT "orders"."id" AS "id", COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE "payments"."status" = 'failed') AS "failed_count" FROM "orders" AS "orders" JOIN "payments" AS "payments" ON "orders"."id" = "payments"."order_id" WHERE "orders"."status" <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY "orders"."id" HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE "payments"."status" = 'failed') > 0) AS "orders_with_failures" LIMIT 1000
